title: Mixed-priority batch creation
description: Probes whether the agent correctly varies a per-item field (priority) within a single batch creation request, rather than collapsing everything to one value or issuing one call per task. RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-25 (netadvanced/vikunja-mcp#28 C1): optimalCallCount reasoning at the time -- create-project (1) + bulk-create 6 tasks with per-task `priority` values in the same call (1) = 2, with setup-kanban deliberately NOT credited because reaching 1 call that way required fabricating an unrequested Kanban board. RE-BASELINED 2026-09-02 (issue #202): that premise is stale -- `setup-kanban`'s `columns` argument became optional (issue #185) two days after the 2026-07-25 note above, and its columns-less form (`title` + `tasks`, no `columns` key at all) creates a project and its tasks in ONE call while resolving/touching ZERO Kanban view or bucket (see labels-due-date-combo.json's description for the precedent: 'its columns-less form is a plain project+tasks composite'). Crediting it here does not erode this scenario's signal: the agent still has to vary `priority` per task within the SAME single call's `tasks` array, whether that call is `bulk-create` or `setup-kanban` -- the property under test (per-item field variation within one call, not one value or one call per task) is identical either way. New optimum: setup-kanban with title + 6 tasks, each carrying its own `priority`, no `columns` (1). A haiku run already reaches this unprompted (issue #202's evidence table: actual=1 against the old optimum of 2), confirming the floor is genuinely reachable.
promptTemplate: Create a project called "{{prefix}}Feature Backlog" with 6 tasks: two low priority (priority 1) called "{{prefix}}low-N", two medium priority (priority 3) called "{{prefix}}med-N", and two high priority (priority 5) called "{{prefix}}high-N" (N=1..2 within each group).
